questions.question: Which property most definitively distinguishes a suspension from a colloid?

options.text: Absence of light scattering under illumination
Settling of particulates under gravitational force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Settling of particulates under gravitational force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the solute-like particles settle out of the solvent-like phase some time after their introduction.
 
• The most definitive distinction is that the particles in a **suspension** will eventually **settle** at the bottom of the container due to **gravitational force** (sedimentation) if left undisturbed. In contrast, **colloidal particles** are small enough that **Brownian motion** counteracts gravity, keeping them suspended indefinitely. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Both suspensions and colloids are technically **heterogeneous mixtures**. While a colloid might appear **homogeneous** to the naked eye, it consists of distinct phases at the microscopic level. Therefore, **homogeneity** does not definitively distinguish them. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Tyndall effect**, or the **scattering of light** by particles, is a property shared by both colloids and suspensions (though very dense suspensions might simply block light). Since both can scatter light, the absence of scattering is not a distinguishing feature of a suspension. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The formation of **covalent solute-solvent bonds** describes a chemical reaction rather than a physical mixture. Both suspensions and colloids are **physical mixtures** where components are held by physical interactions, not **covalent bonds**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Particle Size**:
 
 
• In a **true solution**, the particle size is less than **1 nm**.
 
• In a **colloid**, the particle size ranges between **1 nm and 1000 nm**.
 
• In a **suspension**, the particle size is generally greater than **1000 nm** (or **1 micrometer**), making them visible to the naked eye.
 
 
 
• **Filtration**:
 
 
• Particles of a **suspension** are large enough to be trapped by ordinary **filter paper**.
 
• **Colloidal** particles pass through standard filter paper but can be separated using **ultrafilters** or semi-permeable membranes.
 
 
 
• **Stability**:
 
 
• A **suspension** is considered **unstable** because its phases separate over time.
 
• A **colloid** is relatively **stable**; the particles do not settle down even when left undisturbed for a long period.
 
 
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• Common examples of **suspensions** include **muddy water**, a mixture of **chalk and water**, or **flour in water**.
 
• Common examples of **colloids** include **milk**, **fog**, **blood**, and **mayonnaise**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brownian Motion**: This is the random, **zigzag motion** of colloidal particles resulting from collisions with molecules of the **dispersion medium**. This motion is a key reason why colloids do not settle under **gravity**.
 
• **Tyndall Effect**: Named after **John Tyndall**, this effect allows us to see the path of a light beam as it passes through a colloid or suspension. It is a widely used test in **laboratories** to differentiate a **true solution** from a **colloid**.
 
• **Centrifugation**: While colloidal particles do not settle under normal **gravitational force**, they can be forced to settle using a **centrifuge**, which applies a much higher force. This is how **cream** is separated from **milk**.
 
• **Classification**: Colloids are classified based on the state of the **dispersed phase** and the **dispersion medium** into categories such as **aerosols**, **foams**, **emulsions**, **sols**, and **gels**.
</ul

questions.question: What happens to biodegradable substances when they are released in the environment?

options.text: They get broken down into simpler components.
They get converted into toxic chemicals.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They get broken down into simpler components**__.

• When these substances are released into the environment, biological processes involving **enzymatic actions** convert complex **organic matter** into simpler **inorganic forms** like **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and **minerals**. ***Hence, the statement that they get broken down into simpler components is correct.***
 
• This natural process ensures that nutrients are returned to the **soil** or **atmosphere**, maintaining the **biogeochemical cycles** and the overall **ecological balance** of the planet.
 
• The rate of **decomposition** varies depending on the **nature of the substance** and environmental factors such as **temperature**, **moisture**, and **oxygen availability**.

questions.question: What is the purpose of enrichment of ore before extraction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To remove impurities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Enrichment of ore, also known as **concentration** or **ore dressing**, is the process of removing unwanted materials from the mined ore.
 
• Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with large amounts of impurities such as **soil, sand, and rocky materials**.
 
• These unwanted impurities present in the ore are collectively called **gangue** or **matrix**. ***Hence, the primary purpose is to remove these impurities (Statement 1 is correct).***
 
• The removal of gangue is essential because it increases the **percentage of the metal** in the ore, making the subsequent extraction processes like **reduction** more economical and efficient.
 
• The procedures used for enriching the ore depend upon the difference between the **physical or chemical properties** of the ore and the gangue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Methods of Ore Enrichment:**
 
 
• **Hydraulic Washing:** This is based on the difference in **specific gravities** of the ore and the gangue particles. It is a type of **gravity separation** where an upward stream of running water is used to wash away lighter gangue particles from the heavier ore.
 
• **Magnetic Separation:** This method is employed when either the ore or the gangue possesses **magnetic properties**. For example, **iron ores** like **magnetite (Fe3O4)** are separated from non-magnetic impurities using magnetic rollers and belts.
 
• **Froth Flotation Process:** This technique is specifically used for the enrichment of **Sulphide ores** (e.g., **Galena, Copper pyrites, Zinc blende**). It is based on the **differential wetting** characteristics of the ore and gangue with **water and pine oil**.
 
• **Leaching:** This is a **chemical method** used if the ore is soluble in a suitable solvent. For instance, in the **Bayer process**, **Bauxite** (aluminum ore) is treated with hot concentrated **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** to dissolve the alumina, leaving behind impurities like **Ferric oxide and Silica**.
 
 
 
• **Extraction Sequence:**
 
 
• The process of obtaining a pure metal involves several steps: **Crushing and Grinding** of ore, **Enrichment/Concentration**, **Conversion to Oxide** (via Calcination or Roasting), **Reduction to metal**, and finally **Refining**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Metallurgy:** This refers to the entire **scientific and technological process** used for the isolation of the metal from its ores.
 
• **Mineral vs. Ore:** Naturally occurring chemical substances in the earth's crust are called **minerals**. A mineral from which a metal can be extracted **conveniently and profitably** is called an **ore**.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Proper enrichment reduces the volume of material that needs to be heated in furnaces, thereby **saving energy** and reducing **carbon emissions** during the smelting process.
 
• **Dates and Facts:** The development of modern flotation techniques dates back to the **early 20th century**, which revolutionized the mining industry by allowing the processing of **low-grade ores** that were previously considered waste.
</ul

questions.question: The newton (N) is the SI unit of force. Which of the following expresses one newton (N) in terms of the fundamental SI units (kilogram, metre and second)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kg.m/s2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Newton (N)** is the **International System of Units (SI)** derived unit of **force**. It is named after **Sir Isaac Newton** in recognition of his work on classical mechanics, specifically his **Second Law of Motion**.
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the force acting on an object is equal to the **mass** of the object multiplied by its **acceleration** (**F = m × a**).
 
• In terms of **fundamental SI units**, **mass** is measured in **kilograms (kg)** and **acceleration** is measured in **metres per second squared (m/s2)**.
 
• By substituting these fundamental units into the formula, **1 Newton** is defined as **1 kg × 1 m/s2**. Therefore, **1 N = 1 kg.m/s2**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• One **Newton** is specifically defined as the amount of **force** required to accelerate a mass of **one kilogram** at the rate of **one metre per second squared** in the direction of the applied force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The **dimensional representation** of force is **[M1 L1 T-2]**, where **M** stands for mass, **L** for length (metre), and **T** for time (second).
 
• **Relationship with CGS Units:** In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second (CGS)** system, the unit of force is the **dyne**. One **Newton** is equivalent to **100,000 dynes** (**1 N = 10⁵ dyne**).
 
• **Derived Units involving Newton:** The **Newton** is used to define other derived units such as the **Joule** (unit of **energy** or **work**), which is **1 Newton-metre (N.m)**, and the **Pascal** (unit of **pressure**), which is **1 Newton per square metre (N/m2)**.
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:** While **mass** is a scalar quantity measured in **kilograms**, **weight** is a **force** exerted by gravity on an object and is measured in **Newtons**. On **Earth**, a mass of **1 kg** has a weight of approximately **9.807 N** due to standard **acceleration of gravity**.
 
• **Vector Nature:** Force is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The unit **Newton** quantifies the magnitude of this vector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fundamental SI Units:** There are **seven base units** in the **SI system**: **metre (m)** for length, **kilogram (kg)** for mass, **second (s)** for time, **ampere (A)** for electric current, **kelvin (K)** for thermodynamic temperature, **mole (mol)** for amount of substance, and **candela (cd)** for luminous intensity.
 
• **Force Components:** When expressing **Newtons** in terms of base units, it is essential to remember that **acceleration** itself is a derived unit (**velocity/time**), where velocity is **displacement/time**. This results in the **time squared (s2)** appearing in the denominator of the **Newton** expression.
 
• **Historical Context:** The name "Newton" was adopted by the **General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)** in **1948** as the official name for the **MKS (Metre-Kilogram-Second)** unit of force.

questions.question: To get a virtual, erect and enlarged image using a spherical mirror, the object must be placed _____________.

options.text: at the principal focus (F) of a convex mirror
at the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror
at the centre of curvature (C) of a concave mirror
between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an **inwardly curved reflecting surface**. It has the unique ability to produce both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object.
 
• When an object is placed **between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F)** of a **concave mirror**, the reflected rays diverge. When produced backwards, they appear to meet behind the mirror, forming a **virtual, erect, and enlarged image**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In the case of a **convex mirror**, the image formed is **always virtual, erect, and diminished**, no matter where the object is placed. It cannot produce an enlarged virtual image. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• If an object is placed at the **principal focus (F)** of a **concave mirror**, the reflected rays emerge parallel to each other. This results in an image formed at **infinity**, which is **real, inverted, and highly enlarged**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• When the object is positioned at the **centre of curvature (C)** of a **concave mirror**, the image is formed exactly at **C**. This image is **real, inverted, and the same size** as the object. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **nature of the image** (real or virtual) is determined by whether the light rays actually intersect or only appear to intersect after reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror (Converging Mirror):**
 
 
• These mirrors **converge** light rays falling on them. They are used in **torches, searchlights, and vehicle headlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light.
 
• In the field of medicine, **dentists** use concave mirrors to see **enlarged images** of the teeth of patients.
 
• Large concave mirrors are also utilized to concentrate **solar energy** in solar furnaces.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror (Diverging Mirror):**
 
 
• These mirrors **diverge** light rays. They are commonly used as **rear-view (wing) mirrors** in vehicles.
 
• They are preferred because they always give an **erect, though diminished, image** and have a **wider field of view** as they are curved outwards.
 
 
 
• **Important Optical Terms:**
 
 
• **Pole (P):** The center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** The point on the principal axis where parallel rays of light **converge** (concave) or appear to **diverge** from (convex) after reflection.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the **Pole** and the **Principal Focus**. The radius of curvature (R) is twice the focal length (**R = 2f**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between the object distance (**u**), image distance (**v**), and focal length (**f**) is expressed as **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (**m = h'/h**). It is also related to distances as **m = -v/u**.
 
• For a **virtual and erect image**, the magnification (**m**) is always **positive**. In the case of the object between P and F of a concave mirror, **m > 1** because the image is enlarged.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the focal length of a **concave mirror** is **negative**, while that of a **convex mirror** is **positive**.
</ul

questions.question: The phenomenon in which different parts of the plant, like root, stem and leaves, develop into new plants under appropriate conditions is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vegetative propagation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** in plants where new individual plants are produced from the **vegetative parts** of the parent plant, such as **roots, stems, or leaves**.
 
• In this process, the offspring produced are **genetically identical** to the parent plant, essentially acting as **clones**. This ensures that desirable characteristics of the parent are preserved in the next generation.
 
• Unlike sexual reproduction, this phenomenon does not involve the **fusion of gametes** or the **production of seeds**. It allows plants to reproduce even if they have lost the ability to produce viable seeds.
 
• The process occurs under **appropriate environmental conditions** (moisture, temperature, and nutrients), where specialized structures like **buds** present on the vegetative parts develop into **adventitious roots** and shoots. ***Hence, the correct answer is Vegetative propagation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sexual Reproduction:** 
 
 
• This method involves the **fusion of male and female gametes** (pollen and ovules) to produce a **zygote**, which eventually develops into a **seed**.
 
• It results in **genetic variation** among the offspring, which is crucial for evolution and adaptation to changing environments. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fertilisation:** 
 
 
• **Fertilisation** is the specific biological process of the **union of a sperm cell with an egg cell**.
 
• In flowering plants (**Angiosperms**), this occurs within the **ovary** after **pollination**. It is a step within the cycle of sexual reproduction rather than the name of the propagation method itself. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Regeneration:** 
 
 
• **Regeneration** is the ability of an organism to **regrow lost or damaged body parts**. While some simple organisms like **Hydra** or **Planaria** can give rise to a whole new individual from a small fragment, in the context of higher plants developing from roots/stems/leaves, the term vegetative propagation is more appropriate. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Methods of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• **Natural methods** include **tubers** (Potato), **rhizomes** (Ginger), **runners** (Strawberry), and **bulbs** (Onion).
 
• **Artificial methods** are widely used in **horticulture** and include **cutting** (Rose), **grafting** (Mango), and **layering** (Jasmine).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Plants raised by this method can bear **flowers and fruits earlier** than those produced from seeds.
 
• It is the only method for reproducing plants that do not produce seeds, such as **banana, orange, rose, and jasmine**.
 
• The **uniformity** of the crop is maintained since all plants are **clones** of the parent, which is highly beneficial for **commercial farming** and **agriculture**.
 
• One notable example is the **Bryophyllum** plant, which produces **buds** in the margins of its **leaves**; if these leaves fall on moist soil, each bud can develop into a **new plantlet**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is generally produced when a metal reacts with an acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and hydrogen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **metal** reacts with a **dilute acid**, it generally produces a **metal salt** and **hydrogen gas**. This is a characteristic chemical property of most reactive metals.
 
• In this chemical process, the **metal** displaces the **hydrogen** atoms from the **acid** molecules. For example, when **Zinc** reacts with **Hydrochloric acid**, **Zinc Chloride** and **Hydrogen gas** are formed. ***Hence, the statement regarding salt and hydrogen gas production is correct.***
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction can be represented as: **Metal + Dilute Acid → Salt + Hydrogen Gas (H2)**.
 
• The evolution of **hydrogen gas** can be tested using a burning splinter. When the splinter is brought near the mouth of the test tube where the reaction is occurring, the gas burns with a characteristic **"pop" sound**.
 
• The rate of this reaction depends on the **reactivity** of the metal. Highly reactive metals like **Sodium (Na)** and **Potassium (K)** react explosively, while less reactive metals like **Iron (Fe)** react more slowly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series influence**: Metals that are positioned above **hydrogen** in the **reactivity series** (like **Magnesium, Aluminum, Zinc, and Iron**) can displace hydrogen from acids. However, metals below hydrogen, such as **Copper (Cu)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**, do not typically react with dilute acids like **HCl** or **H2SO4** to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• **The Nitric Acid Exception**: When metals react with **Nitric acid (HNO3)**, **hydrogen gas** is usually not evolved. This is because **Nitric acid** is a **strong oxidizing agent**. It oxidizes the hydrogen gas produced into **water (H2O)** and itself gets reduced to various nitrogen oxides such as **N2O, NO, or NO2**.
 
• **Exceptions to the Nitric Acid Rule**: Only very dilute **Nitric acid** reacts with **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Manganese (Mn)** to actually evolve **hydrogen gas**.
 
• **Types of Salts**: The type of salt formed depends on the acid used. **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** yields **Metal Chlorides**, **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** yields **Metal Sulfates**, and **Acetic acid** yields **Metal Acetates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Displacement Reaction**: This reaction is a prime example of a **single displacement reaction**, specifically a **redox reaction**, where the metal is **oxidized** (loses electrons) and the hydrogen ions in the acid are **reduced** (gain electrons) to form neutral hydrogen gas.
 
• **Exothermic Nature**: The reaction between a metal and an acid is generally **exothermic**, meaning it is accompanied by the release of **heat energy**. The temperature of the reaction mixture usually rises during the process.
 
• **Practical Application**: This reaction is commonly used in **laboratories** for the **preparation of hydrogen gas** on a small scale, typically using **granulated zinc** and **dilute sulfuric acid**.
 
• **Safety Fact**: Because **hydrogen** is highly **inflammable** and forms explosive mixtures with air, these reactions must be performed with caution in controlled environments.
 
• **Corrosion**: This chemical principle explains why **acidic food substances** (like curd or lemon juice) should not be stored in **copper** or **brass** vessels, as the acid reacts with the metal to produce **toxic salts**.

questions.question: The main reason an echo is NOT heard clearly in a small room is:

options.text: Sound intensity decreases too quickly over short distances
Time interval between original sound and echo is too short

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Time interval between original sound and echo is too short**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sensation of sound persists in our brain for about **0.1 seconds**. This phenomenon is known as the **Persistence of Hearing**.
 
• To hear a distinct **echo**, the reflected sound must reach the ear after the original sound has faded. This means the **time interval** between the original sound and the reflected sound must be at least **0.1 seconds**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In a **small room**, the distance between the source of the sound and the reflecting surface (like a wall) is very short. Consequently, the sound reflects back and reaches the ear in **less than 0.1 seconds**, causing the reflected sound to merge with the original sound.
 
• The **speed of sound** in air is approximately **344 meters per second** at a temperature of **22 degrees Celsius**. To achieve a delay of **0.1 seconds**, the sound must travel a total distance of **34.4 meters** (344 x 0.1).
 
• Since the sound travels to the obstacle and back, the **minimum distance** of the reflecting surface from the source must be half of that total distance, which is **17.2 meters**. Most small rooms do not have a length or width of **17.2 meters**, which is why a clear echo is not heard.
 
• Sound intensity actually remains quite high in small rooms because the sound waves are confined, so the idea that intensity decreases too quickly is factually incorrect. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **frequency** of sound determines the **pitch** but does not change the fundamental requirement of the **0.1-second** time gap for an echo to be distinguished by the human ear. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Sound travels at a constant speed for a given medium and temperature (approx **344 m/s** in air); it does not travel "too slowly" to prevent an echo. If it traveled slower, the time interval would actually increase. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reverberation:** In small rooms, instead of a distinct echo, we often experience **reverberation**. This is the persistence of sound due to **multiple reflections**. If the reflections are too frequent and close together (less than **0.1 seconds**), they blur the original sound, which is common in empty rooms or large halls with poor acoustics.
 
• **Conditions for Echo Formation:**
 
 
• The reflecting surface must be **hard** and large enough (like a tall building or a mountain) to reflect sound waves effectively.
 
• The **distance** between the source and the obstacle must be at least **17.2 meters** (in air at standard temperature).
 
 
 
• **Factors affecting the Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** The speed of sound **increases** with an increase in **temperature**. For every **1 degree Celsius** rise, the speed increases by about **0.6 meters per second**.
 
• **Humidity:** Sound travels **faster** in **humid air** than in dry air because water vapor decreases the density of the air.
 
• **Medium:** Sound travels fastest in **solids**, followed by **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**. For example, the speed of sound in **steel** is approximately **5960 m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Echo:**
 
 
• **SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging):** Used by ships and submarines to detect underwater objects by measuring the **time interval** of reflected **ultrasonic waves**.
 
• **Echolocation:** Animals like **bats** and **dolphins** use echoes to navigate and find prey in the dark or underwater.
 
• **Medical Imaging:** **Ultrasound** (Echocardiography) uses the principle of reflection to create images of internal organs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **minimum distance** required for an echo changes with **temperature**. On a hot day, the **speed of sound** is higher, meaning the sound covers more distance in **0.1 seconds**, thus requiring the reflecting surface to be further away (greater than **17.2 meters**) to hear a distinct echo.
 
• **Acoustic materials:** In cinemas and auditoriums, **soft materials** like carpets, heavy curtains, and perforated fiberboards are used to **absorb sound** and reduce excessive **reverberation**.
 
• The **Law of Reflection** for sound is the same as for light: the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**, and they lie in the same plane.

questions.question: Which statement best describes an olfactory indicator?

options.text: A substance that changes smell in acids and bases
A liquid that changes colour in all solutions
A gas that reacts only with strong acids
A solid that dissolves in both acids and bases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A substance that changes smell in acids and bases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose **odor or smell changes** depending on whether they are mixed with an **acidic or a basic solution**.
 
• The term **"olfactory"** pertains to the **sense of smell**, and these indicators are primarily used in **chemistry laboratories** to test the nature of a particular substance when color-based indicators cannot be used.
 
• In an **acidic medium**, the characteristic smell of these indicators typically **remains the same** or does not disappear.
 
• In a **basic medium**, the characteristic smell of these indicators is usually **destroyed or cannot be detected**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A liquid that changes **color** in solutions refers to **visual indicators** like **Litmus, Phenolphthalein, or Methyl Orange**, but not specifically to olfactory ones. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A gas that reacts only with **strong acids** or a solid that **dissolves** in both media does not define the functional property of an indicator meant for **pH detection** through smell. ***Hence, statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Common Examples of Olfactory Indicators:**
 
 
• **Onion:** When a cloth strip treated with **onion juice** is kept in a **base** like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, the pungent smell of the onion **disappears**. However, in an **acid** like **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, the smell persists.
 
• **Vanilla Essence:** The pleasant smell of **vanilla** vanishes when it is added to a **basic solution**. It retains its smell in **acidic solutions**.
 
• **Clove Oil:** The characteristic smell of **clove oil** also disappears in the presence of a **base** and remains detectable in the presence of an **acid**.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:** Unlike olfactory indicators, synthetic indicators like **Phenolphthalein** are colorless in **acidic** solutions and turn **pink** in **basic** solutions. **Methyl Orange** turns **red** in acids and **yellow** in bases.
 
• **Natural Indicators:** Other natural indicators include **Turmeric** (which stays **yellow** in acid and turns **reddish-brown** in base) and **Red Cabbage juice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Utility for Visually Impaired:** Olfactory indicators are highly significant for **visually impaired students** in science education. Since they cannot observe **color changes** in traditional indicators like **litmus paper**, they rely on the **change in odor** to identify the chemical nature of substances.
 
• **Chemical Reaction:** The change in smell occurs because the **acid or base** reacts with the **organic compounds** responsible for the scent in the indicator, effectively neutralizing or altering the molecules that the **olfactory receptors** detect.
 
• **pH Scale Context:** Indicators are used to determine if a substance has a **pH less than 7 (Acidic)** or a **pH greater than 7 (Basic)**. Olfactory indicators provide a **qualitative** rather than quantitative measure of this property.
</ul

questions.question: What would you call the middle elongated part of the female reproductive part of a flower?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The female reproductive organ of a **flower** is known as the **carpel** or **pistil**, which consists of three distinct parts: the **stigma**, the **style**, and the **ovary**.
 
• The **Style** is the **middle elongated part** of the **carpel** that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Style.***
 
• One of its primary **functions** is to act as a physical barrier or a selective track for the growth of the **pollen tube**, ensuring that only compatible **pollen** reaches the **ovules**.
 
• The **Style** serves as a support structure that elevates the **stigma** to a height where it is more likely to capture **pollen grains** from **pollinators** like insects, birds, or the wind.
 
• During the process of **fertilization**, after a **pollen grain** germinates on the **stigma**, the **pollen tube** must travel through the internal tissues of the **style** to reach the **female gametes** located in the **ovary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stigma:**
 
 
• The **Stigma** is the **terminal** or topmost part of the **carpel**.
 
• Its main **feature** is a **sticky** or feathery surface designed to receive and trap **pollen grains** during **pollination**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **pollen recognition**, where the plant determines if the **pollen** is from the same species and is suitable for germination.
 
 
 
• **Ovary:**
 
 
• The **Ovary** is the **basal swollen part** of the **pistil** situated at the bottom of the **style**.
 
• It contains **ovules**, which house the **egg cells**; after **fertilization**, the **ovules** develop into **seeds** and the **ovary** matures into a **fruit**.
 
• In **Angiosperms**, the **location** of the **ovary** can be **superior**, **inferior**, or **half-inferior** depending on its position relative to other floral parts.
 
 
 
• **Pollen Grain:**
 
 
• A **Pollen grain** is not part of the female reproductive system; rather, it is the **male gametophyte** of **seed plants**.
 
• It is produced within the **anther** of the **stamen** (the male reproductive part).
 
• It contains **generative cells** that eventually produce **male gametes** required for **sexual reproduction** in plants.
 
 
 
• **Pistil vs. Carpel:**
 
 
• A **carpel** is the basic unit of the **gynoecium**. A **pistil** may consist of a single **carpel** (**simple pistil**) or several **fused carpels** (**compound pistil**).
 
• The **Gynoecium** is the collective term for all the female parts of a **flower**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following leads to significant damage to the ozone layer in the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are the primary chemicals responsible for the depletion of the **ozone layer**. These are non-toxic, non-flammable chemicals containing atoms of **carbon**, **chlorine**, and **fluorine**.
 
• When **CFCs** are released into the lower atmosphere, they are extremely stable and do not dissolve in rain. Over several years, they drift upward into the **stratosphere**.
 
• In the **stratosphere**, intense **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** from the sun breaks the chemical bonds in **CFCs**, releasing free **chlorine atoms**.
 
• A single **chlorine atom** can destroy over **100,000 ozone molecules** before it is removed from the upper atmosphere. This catalytic cycle causes a significant thinning of the ozone layer. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***
 
• The global recognition of this damage led to the **Montreal Protocol** in **1987**, an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of substances like **CFCs** and **halons**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Ozone Layer:**
 
 
• The **ozone layer** is a region of high **ozone (O3)** concentration in the **stratosphere**, located approximately **15 to 30 kilometers** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It acts as a shield, absorbing about **97% to 99%** of the Sun's medium-frequency **ultraviolet light (UV-B)**, which otherwise would potentially damage exposed life forms on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Other Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS):**
 
 
• Apart from **CFCs**, other chemicals like **halons** (used in fire extinguishers), **carbon tetrachloride**, **methyl chloroform**, and **hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs)** also contribute to ozone depletion.
 
• The thickness of the ozone layer is measured in **Dobson Units (DU)**. A typical ozone layer thickness is about **300 Dobson Units**.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gases vs. ODS:**
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO2)** and **Methane (CH4)** are major **greenhouse gases** responsible for **global warming** and **climate change**. While they affect the atmospheric temperature profile, they are not the direct cause of the chemical destruction of the ozone layer like **CFCs**.
 
• **Oxygen (O2)** is essential for life and is the precursor for ozone formation in the stratosphere through the **Chapman cycle**, where **UV rays** split **O2** into single atoms that then react with other **O2** molecules to form **O3**.
 
 
 
• **Consequences of Depletion:**
 
 
• Thinning of the ozone layer leads to increased levels of **UV-B radiation** reaching the Earth's surface, which can cause **skin cancer**, **cataracts**, and weakened immune systems in humans.
 
• It also disrupts **terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems**, affecting **phytoplankton** productivity and damaging the early developmental stages of fish, shrimp, and crabs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Antarctic Ozone Hole** was first discovered in the **mid-1980s**. It refers to the severe depletion of ozone that occurs over **Antarctica** during the Southern Hemisphere's spring (**September to November**).
 
• **Polar Stratospheric Clouds (PSCs)** play a critical role in ozone depletion over the poles by providing a surface for chemical reactions that convert benign chlorine compounds into reactive forms.
 
• **World Ozone Day** is celebrated every year on **September 16** to commemorate the date of the signing of the **Montreal Protocol**.
</ul

questions.question:
A stone of mass 500g is raised from ground to a height of 20 m. What is the gain in its potential energy?

(Take g=10 {m/s}² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to others, stresses within itself, electric charge, or other factors. Specifically, **Gravitational Potential Energy** is the energy an object possesses because of its position in a gravitational field.
 
• The formula for calculating the **Gravitational Potential Energy (GPE)** of an object is given by the product of its **mass (m)**, the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, and the **height (h)** above a reference point. The mathematical expression is **PE = m * g * h**.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass of the stone** is provided as **500 g**. To use the standard **SI unit** (Joules), we must first convert the mass into **kilograms (kg)**. Since **1000 g = 1 kg**, the mass **m = 500 / 1000 = 0.5 kg**.
 
• The **height (h)** to which the stone is raised is **20 m**, and the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is specified as **10 m/s2**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **PE = 0.5 kg * 10 m/s2 * 20 m**. The calculation results in **0.5 * 200 = 100**. Therefore, the gain in **potential energy** is **100 J**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 100 J.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy**: In a closed system where only conservative forces (like gravity) are acting, the total **mechanical energy** (the sum of **kinetic energy** and **potential energy**) remains constant. When the stone is raised, **work** is done on it, which is stored as **potential energy**.
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)**: This is the energy of an object due to its **motion**. It is defined by the formula **KE = 1/2 * m * v2**, where **v** is the **velocity**. If the stone were dropped from **20 m**, its **potential energy** would convert back into **kinetic energy** as it falls.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **work done** by the sum of all forces acting on a particle equals the change in the **kinetic energy** of the particle. In this context, the **work done** against gravity to lift the stone is exactly equal to the **gain in potential energy**.
 
• **SI Unit of Energy**: The standard unit for energy and work in the **International System of Units** is the **Joule (J)**. One **Joule** is defined as the amount of **work done** when a force of **one Newton** displaces an object through a distance of **one meter**.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity**: While the standard value of **g** on Earth's surface is approximately **9.81 m/s2**, competitive exams often use **10 m/s2** to simplify calculations. **g** varies slightly depending on the **latitude** and **altitude** of the **location**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit Consistency**: Always ensure that mass is in **kg** and height is in **meters** before calculating energy in **Joules**. Forgetting to convert **grams** to **kilograms** is a common mistake that would lead to an incorrect answer of **100,000 J**.
 
• **Reference Level**: Potential energy is **relative**. In this problem, the **ground** is considered the **zero-energy reference level**. The "gain" refers to the difference between the **potential energy** at **20 m** and the **potential energy** at **0 m**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**, unlike force or velocity which are **vectors**.
 
• **Factors Affecting GPE**: The **potential energy** is directly proportional to **mass**, **height**, and **gravity**. If you double the **mass** or the **height**, the **potential energy** will also double.
</ul

questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 40 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm, such that an image is formed at a distance of X cm from the lens. What is the value of X?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**+40/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the image distance in a lens system, we use the **Lens Formula**, which is given by: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• In this problem, the object is placed at a **distance of 40 cm** from the lens. According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the object distance (**u**) is always taken as **negative**. Therefore, **u = -40 cm**.
 
• The lens provided is a **convex lens** with a **focal length (f) of 10 cm**. For a convex lens, the focal length is always considered **positive**. Thus, **f = +10 cm**.
 
• Substituting these values into the lens formula:
 
 
• **1/10 = 1/v - 1/(-40)**
 
• **1/10 = 1/v + 1/40**
 
 
 
• Rearranging the equation to solve for **1/v**:
 
 
• **1/v = 1/10 - 1/40**
 
• Taking the **LCM** of 10 and 40, which is **40**:
 
• **1/v = (4 - 1) / 40**
 
• **1/v = 3 / 40**
 
 
 
• Therefore, **v = 40/3 cm**. Since the value is positive, the image is formed on the **opposite side** of the lens. ***Hence, the correct answer is +40/3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens:** Also known as a **converging lens**, it is thicker at the center than at the edges. It converges parallel rays of light to a point called the **principal focus**. It is used in **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and for correcting **hypermetropia** (long-sightedness).
 
• **Sign Convention for Lenses:** 
 
 
• The **optical center** is treated as the origin.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are positive, while those measured against it are negative.
 
• The **object** is always placed on the **left** side of the lens, making **u** negative.
 
• For a **convex lens**, **f** is **positive**; for a **concave lens**, **f** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Image:** In this specific case, since **v** is positive, the image is **real and inverted**. Because the absolute value of **v** (approx 13.33 cm) is less than the absolute value of **u** (40 cm), the image is **diminished**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also expressed as **m = v/u** for lenses. 
 
 
• In this problem, **m = (40/3) / (-40) = -1/3**.
 
• The **negative sign** indicates that the image is **inverted**, and the value **1/3** indicates that the image is **one-third** the size of the object.
 
 
 
• **Power of Lens:** The reciprocal of the focal length in meters is called **Power (P)**. **P = 1/f (in meters)**. The **SI unit** is **Dioptre (D)**. For this lens, **f = 0.1 m**, so **P = +10 D**.
 
• **Focal Length Comparison:** If the object is placed beyond **2f** (which is 20 cm in this case), the image always forms between **f and 2f** on the other side. Here, **u = 40 cm** (which is > 20 cm), and **v = 13.33 cm** (which is between 10 cm and 20 cm), confirming the laws of **refraction**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combustion of petrol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **chemical change** is a process where one or more substances are altered into one or more **new and different substances**. This involves a change in the **chemical composition** and the formation of **new chemical bonds**.
 
• **Combustion of petrol**: When petrol (a **hydrocarbon**) burns, it reacts with **oxygen** in the air to produce **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor**. Since entirely new substances are formed and the process is **irreversible** under normal conditions, it is a **chemical change**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• **Mixing salt and water**: When salt is dissolved in water, it forms a **solution**. No new chemical substance is created, and the salt can be recovered through **evaporation**. This is a **physical change**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation of water**: This is a **phase transition** where water changes from a **liquid state** to a **gaseous state**. The chemical formula (**H2O**) remains the same throughout the process. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Ice melting**: This involves a change of state from **solid** to **liquid**. It is a **reversible** process, and the **molecular structure** of the water molecules does not change. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Chemical Changes:**
 
 
• They are usually **irreversible**, meaning the original substance cannot be easily recovered.
 
• New products are formed with different **chemical properties**.
 
• Significant **energy changes** occur, often involving the absorption or release of **heat** or **light**.
 
• Examples include **rusting of iron**, **cooking an egg**, **ripening of fruits**, and **digestion of food**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Physical Changes:**
 
 
• These changes affect the **physical properties** such as shape, size, or **state of matter** (solid, liquid, gas).
 
• They are generally **reversible** in nature.
 
• No **new substance** is produced during the process.
 
• Examples include **breaking glass**, **chopping wood**, **freezing water**, and **sublimation of camphor**.
 
 
 
• **Combustion Reactions:**
 
 
• Combustion is an **exothermic reaction**, meaning it releases **thermal energy**.
 
• The **Flash point** is the lowest temperature at which a liquid (like **petrol**) produces enough vapor to ignite in the air.
 
• In an internal combustion engine, the chemical energy of petrol is converted into **mechanical energy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mass**: In any **chemical change**, the total mass of the **reactants** is equal to the total mass of the **products**, as per the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
 
• **Indicators of Chemical Change**: Look for signs such as **evolution of gas**, **formation of a precipitate**, **change in color**, or a significant **change in temperature**.
 
• **Chemical Equations**: Scientists represent chemical changes using **chemical equations** to show how atoms are rearranged. For example, the combustion of methane is represented as **CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O**.
</ul

questions.question: In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is used as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolytic refining** is a technique used by industries to **purify impure metals** obtained from their ores through chemical reduction processes.
 
• In this setup, a thick rod or block of the **impure metal** is made the **Anode**, which is the **positive electrode**. During electrolysis, the metal atoms from the impure anode lose electrons and enter the electrolyte as ions. ***Hence, the statement that impure metal is used as the Anode is correct.***
 
• A thin strip or sheet of **pure metal** is made the **Cathode**, which is the **negative electrode**. The metal ions from the solution gain electrons at this electrode and get deposited as pure metal. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Cathode is incorrect in the context of the impure metal's placement.***
 
• The **Electrolyte** is a **water-soluble salt** of the same metal that is being refined (for example, **Copper Sulphate** for refining copper). It acts as the medium for ion transport. ***Hence, the statement regarding the Electrolyte is incorrect.***
 
• A **Salt** is a chemical compound used to prepare the electrolyte solution but does not serve as the physical electrode where the impure metal is placed. ***Hence, the statement regarding Salt is incorrect.***
 
• As the **electric current** passes through the electrolyte, the **equivalent amount** of pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode, while the same amount of metal dissolves from the impure anode into the electrolyte.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Metals Refined:** This process is widely used for the purification of metals such as **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, **Nickel (Ni)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Anode Mud:** The **insoluble impurities** present in the impure metal settle down at the bottom of the electrolytic tank, specifically below the anode. These are known as **Anode Mud** or **Anode Sludge**. These often contain precious metals like **Antimony**, **Selenium**, **Tellurium**, **Silver**, **Gold**, and **Platinum**, which can be recovered to offset the cost of the refining process.
 
• **Soluble Impurities:** Impurities that are more **electropositive** than the metal being refined go into the **electrolyte solution** and remain there, not depositing on the cathode.
 
• **Purity Level:** Electrolytic refining is highly efficient and can produce metals with a **purity level** of up to **99.99%**, which is essential for electrical applications (like copper wiring) where high conductivity is required.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Reactions:**
 
 
• At the **Anode (Oxidation)**: The metal (M) loses 'n' electrons to become a cation: **M → Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻**.
 
• At the **Cathode (Reduction)**: The metal cation (Mⁿ⁺) from the solution gains 'n' electrons to become pure metal: **Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻ → M**.
 
 
 
• **Specific Example (Copper Refining):** In the refining of **Copper**, the **Anode** is impure copper, the **Cathode** is a thin plate of pure copper, and the **Electrolyte** is an acidified solution of **Copper(II) Sulphate (CuSO4)**.
 
• **Energy Requirement:** The process requires a continuous supply of **Direct Current (DC)**. The voltage applied is usually low to ensure that only the desired metal ions are discharged at the cathode.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** While effective, the process requires significant **electrical energy** and generates **chemical waste** (spent electrolyte) that must be managed according to environmental regulations.
</ul

questions.question: A straight conductor carrying current is placed parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The force on the conductor will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **straight conductor** carrying an **electric current (I)** is placed in a **uniform magnetic field (B)**, it experiences a mechanical force. This force is mathematically expressed by the formula **F = BIL sin(θ)**.
 
• In this formula, **F** represents the **magnetic force** in **Newtons (N)**, **B** is the **magnetic flux density** in **Tesla (T)**, **I** is the **current** in **Amperes (A)**, **L** is the **length of the conductor** in **meters (m)**, and **θ** is the **angle** between the direction of the current and the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The question states that the conductor is placed **parallel** to the uniform magnetic field. In geometry and physics, **parallel** orientation implies that the **angle (θ)** between the two vectors is **0 degrees**.
 
• According to trigonometric principles, the value of **sin(0°)** is exactly **0**. Substituting this into the force equation gives **F = BIL × 0**, which results in a total force of **zero**. ***Hence, the statement that the force is zero is correct.***
 
• Similarly, if the conductor were placed **antiparallel** (in the opposite direction) to the field, the angle would be **180 degrees**. Since **sin(180°)** is also **0**, the force would remain **zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maximum Force Condition:** 
 
 
• The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire reaches its **maximum value** when the conductor is placed **perpendicular** (at an angle of **90 degrees**) to the magnetic field.
 
• This is because **sin(90°) = 1**, making the force formula **F = BIL**. This configuration is widely used in the design of **electric motors** to maximize torque.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule:** 
 
 
• The direction of the magnetic force can be determined using **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**. When the **forefinger** points in the direction of the **Magnetic Field** and the **middle finger** points in the direction of the **Current**, the **thumb** represents the direction of the **Force (Motion)**.
 
• This rule only applies when the current and field are not parallel, as no force exists in the parallel state.
 
 
 
• **Lorentz Force:** 
 
 
• The force on the conductor is a macroscopic manifestation of the **Lorentz Force** acting on individual moving charges (electrons) within the wire. 
 
• The microscopic formula is **F = q(v × B)**, where **q** is the charge and **v** is the **drift velocity**. If the velocity of the charges is parallel to the magnetic field, the **cross product** is **zero**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field (B):** 
 
 
• A **uniform magnetic field** is one where the **magnetic field strength** and direction are the same at all points in the region. It is often represented by **equidistant parallel lines**.
 
• The **SI unit** of magnetic field is the **Tesla (T)**, named after **Nikola Tesla** in **1960**. Another common unit is the **Gauss (G)**, where **1 Tesla = 10,000 Gauss**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The force is **vectorial** in nature, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• If the current in the conductor is **zero**, the force will be **zero** regardless of the strength of the magnetic field.
 
• The **length (L)** refers to the portion of the conductor that is actually immersed within the **magnetic field** boundaries.
 
• In **1820**, **Hans Christian Orsted** discovered that electric currents create magnetic fields, which eventually led to the understanding of how external fields exert forces on these currents.
</ul

questions.question: The skin on the face is primarily made up of which epithelial tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Squamous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The skin on the face, as with the rest of the body's exterior, is primarily composed of **Stratified Squamous Epithelium**. This tissue consists of multiple layers of flat, scale-like cells known as **squamous cells**. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• This specific type of epithelium is **keratinized**, meaning the outer layers are filled with a tough, protective protein called **keratin**. This makes the facial skin waterproof and resistant to friction and bacterial invasion.
 
• **Ciliated epithelium** contains hair-like projections called **cilia** that help in the movement of particles or fluids. This tissue is typically found in the **respiratory tract** (to move mucus) and **fallopian tubes** (to move the ovum). ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Columnar epithelium** consists of tall, pillar-like cells. It is primarily involved in **absorption** and **secretion** and is found in the lining of the **stomach** and **intestines**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cuboidal epithelium** is made of cube-shaped cells and is commonly found in the **ducts of glands** and **kidney tubules**, where it performs functions related to **secretion** and **absorption**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Epithelial Tissue:** This is one of the **four basic types** of animal tissues. It covers the **external surfaces** of the body, lines **internal organs** and cavities, and forms **glands**. Its primary functions include **protection**, **secretion**, **absorption**, and **filtration**.
 
• **Simple vs. Stratified:** Epithelium is classified based on the number of cell layers. **Simple epithelium** consists of a single layer of cells (ideal for **diffusion** and **filtration**), while **stratified epithelium** consists of two or more layers (ideal for **protection** against mechanical or chemical stress).
 
• **Squamous Cells:** These cells are extremely thin and flat with a **centralized nucleus**. In the **skin**, they are packed tightly to form a barrier. In the **lungs** (alveoli), they facilitate the **exchange of gases** due to their thinness.
 
• **The Epidermis:** The facial skin's outer layer is the **epidermis**, which lacks **blood vessels** (avascular) and relies on the underlying **dermis** for nutrients. It is constantly regenerating, with new cells forming at the **basal layer** and moving upward.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Skin Layers:** The epidermis is divided into five distinct sub-layers: **Stratum corneum**, **Stratum lucidum** (only in thick skin), **Stratum granulosum**, **Stratum spinosum**, and **Stratum basale**.
 
• **Keratinization:** This is the process where cells in the **skin** accumulate **keratin** as they move toward the surface, eventually dying and forming a tough, protective **dead layer**.
 
• **Melanocytes:** Found in the **stratified squamous epithelium** of the skin, these cells produce **melanin**, the pigment responsible for skin color and **UV protection**.
 
• **Cell Junctions:** Epithelial cells are held together by specialized structures like **desmosomes** and **tight junctions**, which provide **structural integrity** and prevent leakages between cells.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following 'indicators' is used to test the nature of solutions besides litmus paper?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turmeric and red cabbage juice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **indicator** is a special substance that changes its color when exposed to an **acidic** or **basic** medium, thereby helping to determine the chemical nature of a solution.
 
• **Turmeric** is a very common **natural indicator**. It contains a yellow pigment called **curcumin**. In **acidic** and **neutral** solutions, turmeric remains **yellow**, but it turns **reddish-brown** when it comes into contact with a **base** (such as soap solution). ***Hence, the option containing turmeric is correct.***
 
• **Red cabbage juice** is another effective **natural indicator** derived from the leaves of red cabbage. It contains **anthocyanin** molecules that change color depending on pH. It turns **red or pink** in **acidic** solutions, **purple** in **neutral** solutions, and **green or yellow** in **basic** solutions. ***Hence, the option containing red cabbage juice is correct.***
 
• Substances like **sand**, **alcohol**, **sugar**, **water**, and **table salt** are not indicators because they do not change color in a predictable way to signify the presence of hydrogen ions (acids) or hydroxide ions (bases).
 
• Other natural indicators include **China Rose (Gudhal)**, which turns **dark pink (magenta)** in **acidic** solutions and **green** in **basic** solutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Indicators:**
 
 
• **Litmus**: Extracted from **Lichens**, it is the most commonly used indicator. It is **purple** in distilled water, turns **red** in **acidic** solutions, and **blue** in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Onion and Vanilla**: These are known as **Olfactory Indicators**. Their **characteristic smell** changes or disappears when mixed with **acids** or **bases**, which is particularly useful for visually impaired students.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:**
 
 
• **Phenolphthalein**: This is a man-made indicator that remains **colorless** in **acidic** solutions but turns **deep pink** in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Methyl Orange**: Another synthetic indicator that shows a **red** color in **acidic** media and a **yellow** color in **basic** media.
 
 
 
• **The pH Scale:**
 
 
• The concept of **pH** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a substance.
 
• The scale ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is considered **neutral** (e.g., **pure water**). A **pH less than 7** indicates an **acid**, while a **pH greater than 7** indicates a **base**.
 
• **Universal Indicator**: This is a mixture of several indicators that shows different colors at different **concentrations of hydrogen ions** in a solution, providing a more precise pH value than simple litmus paper.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction of Acids and Bases**: When an acid and a base react, they undergo a **neutralization reaction** to form **salt and water**. Indicators are often used in **titrations** to find the **equivalence point** of this reaction.
 
• **Everyday Examples**: The **reddish-brown stain** of turmeric on a white shirt turns **yellow** again when washed with plenty of water or treated with an **acid** like **lemon juice**, illustrating the reversible nature of the indicator's color change.
 
• **Anthocyanins**: These are the pigments found in **Red Cabbage**, **Blueberries**, and **Raspberries** that provide their vibrant colors and serve as pH-sensitive chemical sensors.
</ul

questions.question: What distinguishes rough ER (RER) from smooth ER (SER)?

options.text: Absence of proteins in RER, presence in SER

Presence of ribosomes on RER, absence on SER
Presence of chlorophyll on RER, absence on SER

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of ribosomes on RER, absence on SER**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a large, dynamic structure that serves many roles in the cell including **calcium storage**, **protein synthesis**, and **lipid metabolism**. It consists of a network of membranous tubules and flattened sacs called **cisternae**.
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** is named for its rough, granular appearance under an electron microscope, which is due to the presence of **ribosomes** attached to its outer (cytoplasmic) surface. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** lacks these attached **ribosomes**, which gives it a smooth, tubular appearance. It is primarily involved in the **synthesis of lipids**, such as phospholipids and cholesterol.
 
• The **RER** is the site where **protein synthesis** occurs for proteins that are either secreted from the cell, incorporated into the cell's plasma membrane, or sent to an organelle like the **lysosome**.
 
• While **RER** is dominated by **cisternae** (flattened sacs), **SER** is largely composed of a network of **tubules** that are interconnected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Rough ER:**
 
 
• It plays a central role in **protein folding** and **quality control**. Proteins that are misfolded are retained in the **RER** and eventually degraded.
 
• It is involved in **glycosylation**, the process of adding carbohydrate chains to proteins to form **glycoproteins**.
 
• The **RER** is continuous with the **nuclear envelope**, facilitating the transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Smooth ER:**
 
 
• In **liver cells**, the **SER** contains enzymes that catalyze reactions to **detoxify** drugs, metabolic wastes, and harmful chemicals.
 
• It is responsible for the **synthesis of steroid hormones**, such as estrogen and testosterone, in the reproductive organs.
 
• In **muscle cells**, a specialized form of **SER** called the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** regulates **calcium ion concentration**, which is vital for muscle contraction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Membrane Presence:** Both **RER** and **SER** are part of the **endomembrane system** and are composed of **phospholipid bilayers**. Therefore, saying membranes are absent in **RER** is factually wrong. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protein Presence:** Both types of ER contain a variety of **enzymatic proteins** required for their specific metabolic activities. **SER** contains proteins for lipid synthesis, while **RER** contains proteins like **translocons** for ribosome docking. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Chlorophyll Location:** **Chlorophyll** is a pigment found exclusively within the **thylakoid membranes** of **chloroplasts** in plant cells and algae; it is never found in the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Lumen:** The internal space of the ER is known as the **ER lumen** or **cisternal space**. It is distinct from the surrounding **cytosol** and provides a unique environment for chemical modifications.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used to determine the purity of a milk sample?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lactometer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Lactometer** is a specialized instrument used to check the **purity of milk** by measuring its **density** or **specific gravity** relative to water.
 
• It operates on **Archimedes’ principle**, which states that a solid suspended in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the submerged part of the suspended solid.
 
• The instrument consists of a **cylindrical bulb** and a **graduated stem**. When placed in milk, it sinks to a certain level; the depth to which it sinks indicates the **purity** or the extent of **water adulteration**.
 
• Pure milk has a specific gravity range, typically between **1.026 and 1.032**. If water is added to the milk, its density decreases, causing the lactometer to sink deeper, resulting in a lower reading on the scale.
 
• It is widely used in **dairy industries** and by **quality control** agencies to ensure that milk has not been diluted or tampered with before reaching the consumer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermometer**:
 
 
• This instrument is used to measure **temperature** or temperature gradients.
 
• It was significantly developed by **Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit** (who invented the **mercury thermometer** in **1714**) and **Anders Celsius**.
 
• It finds extensive use in **medical diagnostics**, **scientific research**, and **industrial processes** to monitor heat levels.
 
 
 
• **Barometer**:
 
 
• A **Barometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure **atmospheric pressure**.
 
• It was invented by **Evangelista Torricelli** in the year **1643**.
 
• The primary application of a barometer is in **meteorology** for **weather forecasting** and determining altitude in **altimeters**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrometer**:
 
 
• A **Hydrometer** is a general instrument used to measure the **relative density** (specific gravity) of various liquids.
 
• It is usually made of glass and consists of a cylindrical stem and a bulb weighted with **mercury** or **lead shot** to make it float upright.
 
• Applications include measuring the **alcohol content** in spirits, **sugar content** in beverages (saccharometer), and **acid levels** in lead-acid batteries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Milk Density**: The density of **cow milk** usually ranges from **1.028 to 1.030 g/ml**, while **buffalo milk** is denser, ranging from **1.030 to 1.032 g/ml**.
 
• **Adulteration Detection**: Apart from water, other substances like **urea**, **detergents**, and **starch** are sometimes added to milk, but a lactometer primarily detects **volumetric dilution** with water.
 
• **Scientific Context**: The **Specific Gravity** measured by these instruments is a **dimensionless quantity**, representing the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of a reference material (usually water at **4 degrees Celsius**).

questions.question: Cells differ in shape and size according to the work they perform in living organisms. Which of the following correctly compares a cell’s shape with its function?

options.text: Red blood cell – Long and branched, transmits messages
Nerve cell – Round in shape, stores food
Amoeba – Irregular in shape, helps in movement and capturing food
Muscle cell – Flat and disc-shaped, carries oxygen

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba – Irregular in shape, helps in movement and capturing food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a **single-celled organism** that lacks a fixed shape, making it **irregular**. It utilizes temporary finger-like projections called **pseudopodia** (false feet) for **locomotion** and to **capture food** through a process called **phagocytosis**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Red blood cells (RBCs)** are generally **round**, **spherical**, or **biconcave** in shape. This specific **biconcave** structure increases the surface area for the **diffusion of oxygen** and allows them to flow easily through narrow capillaries. They do not transmit messages. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Nerve cells**, also known as **neurons**, are **long and branched**. This structure is specialized for **receiving and transferring messages** (electrical impulses), thereby helping to control and coordinate the working of different parts of the body. They do not store food. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Muscle cells** are typically **spindle-shaped**, meaning they are **long and pointed at both ends**. This shape is optimized for **contraction and relaxation**, which facilitates **physical movement** in living organisms. They are not flat disc-shaped oxygen carriers. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **shape of a cell** is intricately linked to the **specific function** it performs. For instance, the **elongated** nature of some cells allows them to cover distances, while the **flat** or **disc** shape of others may help in protection or transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diversity in Cell Shape:**
 
 
• Cells exhibit a wide variety of shapes, including **polygonal**, **columnar**, **cuboid**, **thread-like**, and even **irregular**.
 
• In humans, **White Blood Cells (WBCs)** like **Leucocytes** also have the ability to change their shape, which helps them move through **blood vessel walls** to reach sites of infection.
 
• In plants, **guard cells** of the **stomata** are **kidney-shaped** (or bean-shaped) to regulate the opening and closing of pores for **gas exchange**.
 
 
 
• **Components Affecting Shape:**
 
 
• Components of the cell are enclosed in a **membrane**. This membrane provides **shape** to the cells of plants and animals.
 
• In **plant cells**, an additional covering called the **cell wall** is present outside the cell membrane, which provides **rigidity** and a **fixed shape** to the cells.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Functions:**
 
 
• **Sperm cells** have a **long tail** (flagellum) that enables **motility** to reach the egg for fertilization.
 
• **Skin cells** are often **flat and packed closely** together to form a protective **barrier** for the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cell Size Facts:**
 
 
• The **smallest cell** is **0.1 to 0.5 micrometre** in size, found in **Bacteria** (specifically **Mycoplasma**).
 
• The **largest cell** is the **egg of an ostrich**, measuring about **170 mm × 130 mm**.
 
• The size of the cells has **no relation** to the size of the body of the animal or plant. For example, **nerve cells** in both an elephant and a rat are **long and branched** and perform the same function of **transferring messages**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of Cell:**
 
 
• Cells were first discovered and named by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** while observing a thin slice of **cork** under a primitive microscope.
 
• He observed **box-like compartments** that reminded him of small rooms (cells) in a monastery.
